candidate.fact: items_g2.prc is stored in cents; do not generalize this to items_g1.prc, which is stored in dollars.
candidate.status: Structural candidate from source SQL, not observed transfer effects.

selected_source_records.question: Among electronics reviews with a review body longer than 500 characters, considering only products whose list price is at most $40, what percentage are 1-star? Round to 2 decimal places.
selected_source_records.sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 *
                    SUM(CASE WHEN f.rtg = 1.0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2)
                FROM fdbk_g2 f
                JOIN items_g2 i ON f.ref_id = i.ref_id
                WHERE f.body IS NOT NULL AND LENGTH(f.body) > 500
                AND i.prc IS NOT NULL AND i.prc > 0 AND i.prc <= 4000
selected_source_records.notes: Joins reviews to items; electronics list prices in cents ($40 = 4000). LENGTH on body, conditional percentage.

selected_source_records.question: How many electronics products priced above $50 have at least 5 reviews and an average review rating below 3.0?
selected_source_records.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
                    SELECT i.ref_id
                    FROM items_g2 i
                    JOIN fdbk_g2 f ON i.ref_id = f.ref_id
                    WHERE i.prc > 5000 AND i.prc IS NOT NULL
                    GROUP BY i.ref_id
                    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 AND AVG(f.rtg) < 3.0
                )
selected_source_records.notes: Requires JOIN + GROUP BY + HAVING with two conditions (count threshold AND avg rating threshold), plus cents-to-dollars. Can't be one-shotted without understanding the aggregation pattern.

selected_source_records.question: What is the average review rating given to office products that cost more than $50?
selected_source_records.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(f.rtg), 2)
                FROM fdbk_g1 f
                JOIN items_g1 i ON f.ref_id = i.ref_id
                WHERE i.prc > 50
selected_source_records.notes: Requires JOIN between items and reviews. Agent must discover price column and FK.
